question: Can a one-step differentiable bilevel search over individual neuron gates and per-neuron activation choices compress MLPs and CNNs while retaining classification accuracy more cheaply than topology-oriented DARTS?

key_findings.claim: The three proposed searches differ only in which continuously relaxed unit-level choices are optimized: neuron retention, activation identity, or both.
key_findings.evidence: NAS-NG multiplies each hidden neuron or convolutional channel by a sigmoid gate. NAS-MA uses a softmax mixture over None, Identity, ReLU, Leaky ReLU, tanh, sigmoid, and SiLU for every neuron. NAS-NGMA combines both variables. A one-step DARTS-style hypergradient updates architecture variables on validation loss and weights on training loss; the final network thresholds gates and takes the largest activation coefficient.

key_findings.claim: On twelve overparameterized MNIST MLP starting configurations, neuron gating removes most parameters with essentially no average accuracy loss and is about forty times faster to search than activation-based variants.
key_findings.evidence: The dense configurations average 98.56% test accuracy and 8.97 million parameters. NAS-NG averages 98.53% and 1.90 million parameters, a 78.8% reduction, after 0.45 plus or minus 0.14 search hours. NAS-MA averages 98.50% and 4.64 million parameters after 18.80 plus or minus 12.04 hours; NAS-NGMA averages 98.55% and 3.54 million after 18.81 plus or minus 11.89 hours.

key_findings.claim: MNIST CNN compression reaches 72-75% for gating-based methods while test accuracy remains within roughly one tenth of a point of the dense networks.
key_findings.evidence: For the three-layer CNN, the 99.60% baseline is compared with 99.63% NAS-NG at 73.5% fewer parameters and 99.61% NAS-NGMA at 75.4% fewer. For the four-layer CNN, the 99.62% baseline is compared with 99.50% NAS-NG at 74.7% fewer and 99.56% NAS-NGMA at 72.3% fewer. Mixed activation alone compresses less, 50.5-55.1%.

key_findings.claim: On CIFAR-10, all three unit-level searches outperform the paper's vanilla DARTS run and yield much smaller networks, but remain below the dense baseline and are not compared under a matched architecture space.
key_findings.evidence: After retraining, NAS-NG scores 85.60 plus or minus 0.21% with a 91.4% parameter reduction, NAS-MA 84.55 plus or minus 0.31% with 85.4% reduction, and NAS-NGMA 84.73 plus or minus 0.18% with 92.8% reduction; DARTS scores 82.03 plus or minus 0.50%. The dense baseline reaches 86.14 plus or minus 0.22%. The proposed search starts from a fixed three-convolution-layer network, whereas DARTS searches operations in an eight-cell normal/reduction topology, so the comparison changes both macro-architecture and search space.

key_findings.claim: Neuron gating continues to compress much larger hand-built MLPs and CNN heads, indicating that its favorable MNIST result is not restricted to the original twelve configurations.
key_findings.evidence: A six-layer 193.66-million-parameter MLP is reduced to 12.97 million while test accuracy moves from 98.64% to 98.73%. Three larger CIFAR CNN-plus-MLP-head baselines shrink from 84.11/44.24/25.88 million to 19.37/10.39/6.13 million parameters while accuracy increases from 88.45/88.66/88.86% to 89.38/89.67/89.22%.

key_findings.claim: The evidence favors the simplest gating variant over joint activation search: mixed activations add large search cost without a consistent accuracy or compression gain.
key_findings.evidence: Across the main MLP and CNN tables, NAS-NG searches in less than an hour while MA and NGMA often take about 4.6-18.8 hours; on CIFAR-10 they take about 10 hours versus 0.56 hours for NG during search. NGMA sometimes finds the best accuracy-to-parameter point, but average gains are inconsistent and the paper itself recommends NG as the practical starting point.

method.core_idea: Turn neuron count and activation assignment into differentiable validation-level variables inside an oversized network, optimize them with a DARTS-style bilevel approximation, discretize the resulting supernet, and retrain the selected compact architecture from scratch.
method.mechanism: NG places an unconstrained scalar on each hidden neuron or channel and maps it through a sigmoid gate. MA attaches seven activation logits to each unit and computes a softmax-weighted activation mixture, with the None operation able to deactivate a unit. NGMA gates the mixture. At every search iteration, architecture parameters receive a validation-loss hypergradient through one lower-level gradient step; weights receive a training-loss update. Search uses half of the nominal training set for weights and half for architecture selection. At termination, a prescribed but numerically unspecified gate criterion determines retention, activation argmax determines the discrete operation, and the derived network is trained anew.
assumptions: An oversized fixed-depth starting network contains a high-performing compact subnet, so width pruning is sufficient for the intended deployment tradeoff.
One-step unrolling is an adequate approximation to the lower-level optimum in the bilevel problem.
Sigmoid gate magnitude and softmax activation magnitude predict the importance of a unit or operation after discretization and retraining.
Validation loss under a weight-sharing mixed supernet preserves the ranking of discrete architectures trained from scratch.
Parameter count is an adequate proxy for deployment efficiency despite hardware-dependent activation latency, memory access, and sparsity structure.
Fixed hyperparameters are comparably suitable for NG, MA, NGMA, and DARTS even though their optimization dynamics and search spaces differ.

techniques.role: Relaxes each unit's keep-or-prune decision into a trainable scalar multiplier.
Searches a seven-operation activation distribution independently at each hidden neuron or convolutional channel.
Updates architecture variables on held-out validation loss through one approximate lower-level weight step.
Thresholds learned gates and selects activation argmaxes to turn continuous search variables into a deployable network.
Separates final architecture quality from weights inherited during search.
Applies gating to networks up to 193.66 million parameters and to DARTS-derived cells to test complementary width refinement.

evaluations.result: NAS-NG 98.53% mean, 98.60% max, 1.90M parameters, 78.8% reduction, and 0.45 plus or minus 0.14 hours
evaluations.baseline: Dense mean 98.56%, max 98.69%, 8.97M parameters; MA and NGMA take about 18.8 hours

evaluations.result: NG 77.59 plus or minus 0.31%, 0.56 plus or minus 0.02 hours, 0.49 plus or minus 0.04M parameters

limitations: Author-stated: MNIST is near ceiling and can hide meaningful architectural differences; CIFAR-10 only partially addresses this, and ImageNet-scale evidence is absent.
Author-stated: MLP experiments vary only depth and width, leaving dropout, batch normalization, skip connections, and other architectural interactions unexplored.
Author-stated: hyperparameters are held fixed rather than independently tuned for each method, limiting cross-method precision.
Author-stated: selected networks are retrained from scratch, so weight inheritance and knowledge distillation are not studied.
Reviewer-identified: the gate threshold or pruning criterion is never given numerically, preventing exact reconstruction of the discrete architecture from learned gates.

Reviewer-identified: the formal MA method is a learned seven-operation mixture, but the results prose repeatedly describes activation-magnitude statistics gathered over data; this inconsistency leaves the implemented pruning rule ambiguous.
Reviewer-identified: CIFAR comparisons with DARTS are not search-space matched: channel pruning of a fixed three-layer CNN is contrasted with operation and topology search in an eight-cell network.

Reviewer-identified: means and standard deviations are reported, and fixed random seeds are mentioned, but the number and identity of independent seeds are not clearly documented for each table; MNIST means also aggregate heterogeneous starting architectures.
Reviewer-identified: no FLOPs, measured inference latency, energy, peak memory, or target-device benchmark supports the deployment claims; unstructured neuron counts need not predict real speed.
Reviewer-identified: the paper claims natural extension to RNNs and Transformers without experiments on either family.
failure_modes: Architecture-parameter magnitude may not reflect causal contribution, so thresholding or argmax can discard useful units and operations despite low supernet validation loss.
The soft mixed-activation supernet can exploit combinations that no single argmax activation reproduces after discretization.
Sigmoid gates can remain clustered near an arbitrary threshold, making architecture size unstable to small optimizer or seed changes.
A None activation and a separate neuron gate create redundant ways to remove a unit in NGMA, weakening identifiability and conditioning.
One-step bilevel gradients can favor short-horizon validation improvements instead of architectures that train well to convergence.
Easy or highly overparameterized tasks make nearly any pruning heuristic look effective once minimum capacity is retained.
Accuracy divided by parameter count becomes numerically extreme for tiny networks and can reward impractical models without reflecting latency or memory bandwidth.
Changing both the search space and macro-architecture can make a DARTS baseline look worse for reasons unrelated to the proposed optimizer.
Activation mixtures multiply search compute and memory per unit; on large models, the seven-way relaxation can become less scalable than the discrete problem it replaces.
Fixed per-method hyperparameters can systematically undertrain a competitor or over-regularize one relaxation.
reusable_insights: Treat width and activation assignment as separate search axes before paying the cost of a joint relaxation; here the cheap width axis captures most of the gain.
Retrain discrete architectures from scratch to audit whether a weight-sharing supernet found structure rather than merely favorable inherited weights.
Compare NAS methods under the same macro-architecture, primitive operations, compute budget, and hardware metrics before attributing gains to the search rule.
Specify the exact continuous-to-discrete rule and report sensitivity around every gate threshold.
Measure perturbation importance or removal loss in addition to architecture-coefficient magnitude when pruning a differentiable supernet.
Use parameter count as one Pareto coordinate, alongside latency, memory, energy, and accuracy, rather than collapsing them into an accuracy-per-parameter ratio.
Stress-test pruning on oversized networks, but also include capacity-matched dense baselines to determine whether search beats simple width scaling.
open_questions: Does NG outperform magnitude pruning, network slimming, random structured pruning, or a tuned width multiplier under a matched training and compute budget?
How stable are selected neurons, channels, and activation functions across seeds and small gate-threshold changes?
Would perturbation-based discretization repair the known mismatch between architecture-parameter magnitude and operation importance?
Do mixed activations yield device-level speed or energy gains after compiler fusion and kernel availability are considered?
Can a resource-constrained objective search accuracy, latency, and memory jointly instead of optimizing validation loss alone?
Do the reported gains survive ImageNet, sequence modeling, Transformers, distribution shift, and adversarial corruption?
Which result corresponds to the implemented MA rule: softmax activation selection or post hoc activation-magnitude pruning?

competitive_landscape.title: DARTS: Differentiable Architecture Search
competitive_landscape.difference: DARTS introduces continuous operation mixtures and approximate bilevel gradients for cell topology, validating on CIFAR, ImageNet, and recurrent language modeling. This paper reuses that optimization pattern for unit retention and per-neuron activations, but its headline CIFAR comparison uses a different macro-architecture and search space.

competitive_landscape.title: Learning Efficient Convolutional Networks through Network Slimming
competitive_landscape.difference: Network Slimming adds sparsity to batch-normalization scaling factors and prunes channels in VGG, ResNet, and DenseNet. NAS-NG instead learns validation-level sigmoid gates, includes MLP neurons, and retrains the discrete subnet, but does not compare directly with this simpler mature structured-pruning baseline.

competitive_landscape.title: Flexible Channel Dimensions for Differentiable Architecture Search
competitive_landscape.difference: Flexible Channel Dimensions already performs differentiable dynamic channel allocation and evaluates task accuracy, inference latency, GPU-hours, and memory on CIFAR-10. The present paper adds per-neuron mixed activations and fully connected networks, but omits resource-aware objectives and measured device efficiency.

competitive_landscape.title: ActNAS : Generating Efficient YOLO Models using Activation NAS
competitive_landscape.difference: ActNAS searches heterogeneous activation assignments in YOLO and validates accuracy, latency, and memory on CPU, GPU, and NPU hardware. NAS-MA provides a per-neuron softmax bilevel relaxation and can jointly prune units, but is tested only by parameter count and classification accuracy.

competitive_landscape.title: Rethinking Architecture Selection in Differentiable NAS
competitive_landscape.difference: Wang et al. prove and demonstrate that architecture-parameter magnitude need not equal operation importance and improve selection using direct perturbations. That finding directly challenges NAS-NGMA's unexplained gate threshold and activation argmax; this paper supplies no perturbation or discretization-stability ablation.

novelty_assessment: Author claim: the paper introduces three relaxed bilevel formulations for neuron-level gating, mixed activation selection, and their joint use in MLPs and CNNs, with simple searches that rival more elaborate NAS at far lower cost. Differentiable topology search, structured channel pruning, differentiable channel allocation, mixed-activation NAS, and critiques of magnitude-based discretization all predate it. Reviewer inference: the incremental novelty is the common per-neuron bilevel formulation and especially the joint gate-plus-seven-activation search across both dense and convolutional networks. The strongest empirical result is actually the simpler NG compressor, not a new general NAS optimum. Missing threshold details, conflicting MA descriptions, unmatched DARTS spaces, and no hardware or large-scale evaluation substantially weaken claims of scalable deployment superiority.
